items.briefing:
Google Cloud is warning organisations that as AI-based attacks increase, getting the basics right matters more than ever — things like patching systems, strong passwords, and access controls. Separately, a new malware technique called WordlistLoader is hiding malicious code inside ordinary-looking text files, making it harder for standard security tools to detect threats. Publicly available exploit code has also been released targeting flaws in Cudy routers, meaning attackers can easily attempt these attacks.

Ensure your office routers and networking equipment are running the latest firmware updates, and remind staff to be cautious opening unexpected text or document files, even if they look harmless.

featured.title: Foul Language: WordlistLoader Disguises Malware as Ordinary Text
featured.summary: ClickFix-style threat campaigns are using a new trick to evade detection and deliver Amatera, an increasingly prevalent infostealer.
